messages:
marta: Quick sync — thinking through per-org throttle policy (RPM/TPM + concurrency). Need input on console override UX and what telemetry we should emit. TL;DR: customers want predictable bursts + safety net for runaway jobs.

kai: +1. Are we leaning token-based or request-based limits? both have different telemetry needs.

marta: For now we want RPM/TPM as the billing & spike control surface, plus concurrency caps for hot-key protection. Token surface is a separate optimization (post-rollout).

devin: UX note: console teams want a single place to change policy with clear impact preview. e.g., "Increase RPM from 1200 -> 2400" should show estimated 95th latency delta and cost delta.

samir: For enforcement, we should prioritize per-org concurrency at the router layer (reject fast) and do RPM/TPM at the quota service (leaky-window). Concurrency protects capacity, RPM smooths long-run throughput.

leah: On overrides: admins should be able to apply timeboxed bursts (like promo or migration windows) and an emergency toggle that can be applied instantly. UX: two controls — "scheduled bump" and "ephemeral override". Scheduled bumps show a timeline and will be applied with a precheck.

james: Telemetry wishlist: org_id, policy_id, applied_rpm, applied_tpm, observed_rpm, observed_tpm, concurrency_in_use, rejections_by_reason (concurrency|rate|blocked), fallback_route_id. Add sampling of requests that are rejected for postmortem.

marta: good. also want audit trail: who changed what in console, policy versioning, and automatic rollback if errors spike.

kai: Implementation detail — recommend we expose enforcement headers for clients so they can surface bucket state. Example headers:

```
X-Redwood-Rate: org=acme,policy=org-std,rpm=1200,tpm=20000,concurrency=50
X-Redwood-Rate-Remaining: rpm=350,tpm=12345,concurrency=12
X-Redwood-Rate-Reset: rpm=170s,tpm=3600s
```

kai: These help customers gracefully degrade and also let us correlate in traces.

samir: On server-side telemetry, emit meter metrics per org + 1m/5m/1h windows and a counter for bursts used. We should also emit a small sample of full KV cache sizes when concurrency kicks in — helps debug hot keys.

leah: Console preview should run a quick capacity simulation using historical traffic (last 24h) + the requested change and show percent of requests that would have been throttled, plus cost estimate. We can do a dry-run by replaying sampled logs.

devin: Edge case: orgs with many API keys. Do we apply per-org aggregate only or per-org+per-key layered limits? I vote layered: per-key to avoid single-key abuse, per-org to control total spend. Need to display both in console and in telemetry.

marta: Agree layered. Console default shows org aggregate, with an expandable table for top 10 keys and their current caps. Scheduled bump can target org or specific keys.

james: Rollouts: start with soft enforcement mode (headers only + telemetry + log warnings) for 2 weeks, then hard enforcement. We should build a "policy health" dashboard for QA to watch rejections and latency regressions.

marta: Can quota-bot suggest initial policy values? e.g., based on 99th of last-30d * safety factor. quota-bot: please? :smile:

quota-bot: suggested_policy(org=acme): rpm=1500, tpm=22000, concurrency=60 (based on 99th*1.2 over last 30d)

samir: Love that. We'll need an override permission model: who can schedule vs who can emergency-toggle. Map to org admin roles.

leah: UX question: should console show both RPM and "tokens per request" estimate? some customers bill by tokens. Maybe show both but mark token numbers as estimated.

kai: For rollout, add a feature flag per org so we can opt-in beta customers for hard-enforcement. Also plan a migration script to backfill policy_id into past logs for metric continuity.

devin: Open TODOs: 1) finalize header schema, 2) telemetry event names & sampling config, 3) console preview prototype, 4) quota-bot heuristics + permission model.

marta: Awesome. @kai @leah can you sketch the console mock by EOD Wed? @samir @james can you draft the telemetry/event schema? I'll coordinate rollout plan + docs.

kai: Will do.

leah: Yep, mock incoming.

samir: Drafting telemetry now.

james: I'll wire up a draft dashboard in grafana staging.

marta: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
